inputs.text: The Wisconsin case should not end with a simple lesson that citizens must obey the rules while officials are owed unquestioning trust. Harry Wait was convicted of two misdemeanor election-fraud charges and one felony identity-theft charge, and acquitted of another identity-theft count; claiming to expose weaknesses does not make taking ballots in Robin Vos and Cory Mason’s names legitimate oversight. But durable public trust also requires officials to answer questions plainly and make the system open to scrutiny. When institutions treat confidence as something people must provide without transparency, suspicion can deepen—and illegal stunts only make that worse. We need both respect for election law and real accountability from those who run public institutions.
